item.title: HSBC, Citi turn bullish as Indian stocks draw record inflows
item.description: Global banks are turning more positive on Indian stocks, indicating potential for continued growth and record foreign inflows. Recent data shows that India’s benchmark index surged nearly 8% this month, marking its best performance since mid-2022. As foreign investors shift back to Indian equities, analysts expect significant inflows and improved earnings growth in the coming fiscal years. Falling oil prices are also projected to support corporate profits and economic stability.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Global banks are turning more bullish on Indian stocks as the market’s sharpest rally in more than four years draws record foreign inflows.HSBC Holdings Plc lifted local equities to overweight from neutral, citing resilient earnings and more reasonable valuations. Citigroup Inc. raised its 12-month target for the NSE Nifty 50 Index by nearly 8% to 28,000, pointing to improving profit growth and lower oil prices.The calls suggest that Indian equities’ recent rebound may have further to run. The views signal a broader reset in sentiment toward India after a prolonged stretch of underperformance, as investors seek markets less vulnerable to concerns over stretched AI valuations.“India offers diversification and low volatility in Asian markets dominated by AI stocks,” HSBC strategists including Herald van der Linde wrote in a note. They favor banks, industrials, consumer discretionary companies, insurers and hospitals.135673874The benchmark index is up nearly 8% this month, the most since July 2022, making India one of the best-performing major markets globally. Local stocks slipped Monday, bucking a rebound in Asian peers, as investors booked profit following the recent rally.Overseas funds bought a net $3.6 billion of local shares in the four days through Thursday, putting them on course for their biggest-ever weekly inflow. Provisional data showed another $1.5 billion of purchases Friday.The shift marks a sharp reversal after foreign investors spent much of the past two years cutting exposure to India as they chased AI-driven gains elsewhere in Asia and the US. That left positioning relatively light.Citi sees significant scope for foreign positioning to rebuild. A percentage-point increase in active fund allocations to India could generate about $12 billion of inflows, according to analysts including Surendra Goyal and Vijit Jain, after AI “crowded out almost everything else”.The brokerage expects Nifty earnings to grow about 15%-16% annually for fiscal years 2026-2028. It also sees cheaper crude supporting the economy and corporate profits, estimating a $10 decline in oil prices could boost Nifty earnings per share by about 2%.

item.title: Citi bullish on Indian equities, sees Nifty at 28,000 by end-2027
item.description: Citi Research projects that India's benchmark Nifty 50 index could hit 28,000 points by the end of 2027. This forecast is based on strong earnings prospects and falling oil prices. Recent foreign portfolio investor activity has contributed significantly to the positive sentiment in the equity market. Additionally, lower oil prices could improve macroeconomic conditions and reduce inflation rates in India.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brokerage firm Citi Research expects India's benchmark Nifty 50 index to reach 28,000 points by end-2027, citing a strong earnings outlook, lower oil prices and the prospect of slower AI capex as tailwinds for equities in Asia's third-largest economy.The target implies an upside of about 12% from the Nifty 50's last close of 24,986.4.Indian equities have until recently lagged global peers as enthusiasm around the AI trade and elevated crude oil prices weighed on the outlook for the world's third-largest oil importer.Citi's bullish outlook comes after the benchmark Nifty 50 surged more than 10% over the seven sessions through Friday, buoyed by a resurgence of foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) as AI-linked trades unwound and oil prices retreated. Over the past two years, AI has crowded out almost everything else. Our analysis suggests a ~100bp increase in India active weight could drive ~$12bn of inflows, Citi said in its India equity strategy note dated November 8.Sentiment towards Indian equities improved after a Democratic victory in the US midterm elections fuelled expectations of slower AI-related capital expenditure and lower oil prices, on hopes for an end to the conflict involving Iran. Post US mid-terms, risks of increased pace of data center moratoriums has aided rotation into other assets, (and this) could continue to benefit India, Citi said.FPIs have bought Indian shares worth over $4.1 billion so far in November, already their biggest monthly inflows since September 2024.Citi raised its price-to-earnings multiple for Nifty 50 to 18x from 17x, leading to the target of 28,000 points. It earlier expected the 50-stock index at 26,000 by September 2027. Lower oil price could help India's macro and earnings assumptions. A $10 (per barrel) lower oil price would help (current account deficit) by 30-40 bps and inflation by 50 bps, the brokerage firm said.
